validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row US-gas roster and the flagged 'Spire, 2 rows' cluster. P0255 (Spire STL Pipeline) is a real, independently well-documented 65-mile, 24-inch greenfield interstate pipeline built 2018-2019 from an interconnect with Rockies Express Pipeline in Scott County, IL to interconnects with Spire Missouri and Enable MRT (Chain of Rocks) in St. Louis County, MO -- FERC Docket CP17-40, certificated Aug 3, 2018 (164 FERC P 61,085), vacated by the DC Circuit June 22, 2021 (EDF v. FERC, No. 20-1016), and reissued Dec 15, 2022 (Order on Remand and Reissuing Certificates). This is a physically and historically DIFFERENT asset from P2565 (Spire MoGas), an older, pre-existing central-Missouri system Spire acquired years earlier by purchase (previously CorEnergy-owned, per the cluster note) -- no evidence found that P0255 and P2565 were ever the same pipeline under different names, and classification (gas transmission, operating) is correct for P0255. HOWEVER: a major NEW finding materially affects this cluster going forward -- see the attribution concern below on the October 2025 FERC-approved corporate consolidation of the two entities.

The sheet's ConstructionYear=2019 is contradicted by the only two sources found that state an actual construction-start date, both placing it in late 2018, not 2019: (1) pipesak.com, the construction contractor's own project page: 'Spire Energy began construction on the 65-mile, 24 diameter STL Mainline Pipeline in December 2018' -- verified, working URL; (2) FERC's own order in Docket CP17-40-005 (174 FERC P 61,058, 'Order Dismissing Complaint,' issued Jan 19, 2021) states Spire 'accepted its certificate on August 8, 2018, and commenced construction in November 2018' -- I extracted and read this order in full (downloaded, pdftotext-verified) but could NOT obtain a working, citable URL for it despite escalation: ferc.gov/media/ and elibrary.ferc.gov both return 403/require JS-rendered document IDs I could not resolve via curl with either the tool's standard UA or a full browser UA, and this session's web-search budget was exhausted before a working link could be located -- per standing rule 2 I am not fabricating a URL for it, so it is cited here as corroborating context only, not as a proposed_ref. The construction contractor's independently verifiable page alone is sufficient to contradict the sheet's 2019 and support 2018; the FERC order's November-2018 date and the contractor's December-2018 date are consistent with each other (both post-date the Aug 8, 2018 certificate acceptance) even though not identical months. Feb 2019 press (myjournalcourier) describing 'construction began this month' refers only to a specific Elsah, IL directional-drill river crossing, not the overall project start, and does not contradict a Nov/Dec 2018 project-wide groundbreaking. | ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-15: tier/independent corrected (independent). Rule 4 sets `high`/independent at 2+ INDEPENDENT origins; this record's proposed_refs resolve to 1 publisher (pipesak.com). One publisher restated -- and every dated EIA release together -- is still ONE origin..

validity.researcher_notes: MAJOR FINDING, directly responsive to the batch's 'Spire, 2 rows' cluster note. On October 8, 2025, FERC staff issued an order granting a joint application filed June 27, 2025 by Spire MoGas Pipeline LLC and Spire STL Pipeline LLC (Docket CP25-513, per the July 16, 2025 Federal Register notice of that application) 'requesting authorization for: (1) Spire STL to abandon by transfer all of its jurisdictional facilities to Spire MoGas; (2) Spire MoGas to acquire the facilities Spire STL seeks [to transfer]' (thompsonenergyexpert.com, Oct 22, 2025, a specialized FERC-issuances industry newsletter -- the source is paywalled past the lead paragraph, so I could not confirm an implementation/closing date for the transfer, only the grant date). This is a SINGLE-SOURCE finding for the grant itself (I could not find independent press corroboration of the Oct 8, 2025 order before this session's web-search budget was exhausted), corroborated only for the underlying APPLICATION's existence by the July 2025 Federal Register notice (same-origin as the applicant, not independent per this project's independence rule). Given the finding is single-sourced and I have no confirmed completion date, I am NOT changing the Owner1/Operator VALUE in the fills below -- those fills keep 'Spire STL Pipeline LLC,' which is well-documented and correct for the entire 2016-2025 history covered by my other sources. This concern instead flags the pending/likely-completed corporate consolidation for a dedicated Update pass to confirm completion and update Owner1/Operator (and possibly Company/parent fields) on BOTH P0255 and P2565 once a completion date is verified. This is a corporate/ownership change, not a physical-pipeline merger -- I found no evidence the two systems' PHYSICAL infrastructure is being combined (STL interconnects with Rockies Express, Spire Missouri, and Enable MRT; no source names an interconnect with the separate MoGas system), so this stays an attribution issue, not a duplicate/existence issue -- P0255 and P2565 should remain separate rows even after the ownership consolidation.

Per the gem_schema.md gotcha, FuelSource must name a specific upstream producing field/plant/facility, not a fuel type or another pipeline. Every source (FERC order, PSC filing, certificate application, NGI) describes Spire STL's single receipt point as an interconnection with the Rockies Express Pipeline (REX) in Scott County, IL -- REX is itself an interstate PIPELINE (originating in eastern Ohio/Marcellus-Utica producing areas and terminating in Colorado), not a named field or plant. No source attributes the gas to one specific upstream field the way GEM's FuelSource convention expects (e.g., a named Marcellus well pad or gathering facility) -- the gas is generic REX-system supply, commingled from many producers by the time it reaches Spire STL. Leaving blank is correct per the schema rule against filling this with a pipeline name or generic fuel-type description.
